name: Mont-Saint-Michel
tagline: The abbey island rising from the tides of Normandy
summary: Mont-Saint-Michel is a rocky island crowned by a medieval abbey, cut off by some of the biggest tides in Europe. Climb the single village street to the abbey, walk the bay barefoot with a guide at low tide, and pair it with Saint-Malo's walled port and the D-Day beaches of Normandy.
seasonNote: Spring and September are quieter; the big spring tides (around full and new moon) are the most dramatic.
arrival: Trains run from Paris to Rennes or Pontorson, then a bus to the Mont; driving from Paris takes about 4 hours.
gettingAround: Park on the mainland and take the free shuttle or walk 45 minutes across the causeway; a car helps for Saint-Malo and the D-Day beaches.
cashTip: Cards work almost everywhere; service is included in prices, so round up only for good service.
foodTip: La Mère Poulard's puffy omelette, pré-salé lamb from the salt meadows, Cancale oysters and Breton crêpes.
buyTip: Butter biscuits and salted-caramel from the village, and cider and Calvados from Normandy farms.
baseArea: Hotels by the shuttle stop, or stay on the Mont for the evening calm

connections.note: TGV to Rennes, then bus to the Mont.
